about: The held-out lane (.work/phase-9b-heldout.md): programs jz was never tuned on, named here before they are run, measured once on first contact, every program counted and a failure a row.

Written from GitHub metadata alone (names, blob ids, sizes, commits; each licence by GitHub's license API): no program of a set is fetched to a developer's machine or read there, and each driver is written from its set's documented interface. Two were, after their registration and before any contact: clbg-nbody-node-2 and clbg-mandelbrot, fetched on 2026-11-15 and read, not run, to find why V8 did not run them through the harness in the first dry run (run 43777318282); what was found is each one's notMeasured, and the harness's change for it applies to any program so marked. The workflow (.github/workflows/heldout.yml) fetches the pinned files, checks each against its blob id, and is the only writer of the record (bench/heldout.json).

A program's registration is the last commit that changed its line here, a commit that changes no compiler source. Its first contact measures a compiler with no change to compiler source since (test/bench-claims.js computes it from git; a contact run refuses otherwise). A program registered before the compiler's last change is registered again by a commit of its own that changes its registered date, and only while no one has run it with jz.

A program the lane cannot measure, for a reason V8 alone shows and no result of jz's decides (a dry run builds no jz), stays registered and is marked notMeasured, the reason its value. The dry run requires it to fail in V8 and fails when it passes, so a mark ends with its reason; no lane measures it, the record stores no entry of it, and the lane's figures keep it in every denominator, named as not measured. A mark added or removed changes the program's line, and so registers it again.

A program leaves the held-out set the commit after its first contact is stored: a later measurement is stored beside it, marked tuned, never in its place. A release that quotes the lane needs new programs registered for it and measured once.
What no test can hold, the owner keeps: that no one read a program of a set, or ran it with jz, before it was registered here.

sets.about: Every JavaScript program of benchmarks/JavaScript, CommonJS modules bundled with benchmark.js and som.js by esbuild. A program exports newInstance(), whose Benchmark answers innerBenchmarkLoop(innerIterations) true when verifyResult accepts every result (benchmark.js, harness.js). The driver makes one instance, times one innerBenchmarkLoop(inner) a round and hashes every round's answer: the program's own check, in every lane. inner is the innerIterations rebench.conf runs each program at, as recalled, not read here: the dry run prints rebench.conf's lines that name each program beside it.

sets.about: Every .node program of the four problems that read no input, in the Benchmarks Game's CVS repository as mirrored on GitHub (the game's own repository is not on GitHub). A program reads its size from process.argv[2] and prints its answer with console.log or process.stdout.write. The driver runs its source as the body of a function, against that host injected by esbuild (bench/heldout/shim.js), times one whole run a round at arg, and hashes every character or byte the run printed. arg is chosen for 20 to 200 ms a round in V8 from the problems' published sizes, not measured here. The set's own check is its <n>_out file, the output at n.

programs.notMeasured: a script of sloppy mode: it assigns n and runTest, names it never declares (n = +process.argv[2]; runTest = function(n) {…}), which a script makes globals of and an ES module, strict, refuses with a ReferenceError; every lane runs the driver as an ES module, and declaring the names would rewrite the program

it spreads its work over processes: require('cluster') forks os.cpus().length * 2 workers of the running script, which send their rows back by process.send for the master to write, where a lane runs one program in one process
